rendered:

The review mentions that the Haber-Bosch process achieves an energy eﬃciency of 60% under optimized conditions, and that Li-NRR currently has an energy eﬃciency ranging from 1-17%. 

Assuming an average energy eﬃciency of 10% for Li-NRR, and an energy eﬃciency of 60% for the Haber-Bosch process, we can estimate the ratio of the energy required for Li-NRR to the energy required for the Haber-Bosch process.

Energy ratio = (1/0.1) / (1/0.6) = 6

This means that Li-NRR requires 6 times more energy than the Haber-Bosch process. 

The cost of production is directly proportional to the energy required, so if the energy required for Li-NRR is 6 times higher than for the Haber-Bosch process, the production cost per tonne of ammonia for Li-NRR would also be 6 times higher. 

However, this is a very rough estimate and the actual production cost per tonne of ammonia for Li-NRR could be much higher or lower, depending on various factors such as the cost of materials, the capital cost of the equipment, and the cost of electricity.
